title: JPMorgan says cyberattack on third-party vendors may have exposed some customer data
date_note: Published November 19; date of the vendor attack not stated.
summary: JPMorgan said in a statement on Thursday 19 November that third-party service providers were attacked and it believes attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses. It says there is no disruption to its services and no connection to the disruption some customers saw earlier in the week. It did not say when the attack happened or name the vendors.
plain: JPMorgan says outside companies it uses were hacked, and some customers' names and email addresses may have been exposed.
exec: Vendor-held customer contact data is a phishing risk and shows how third-party suppliers extend a bank's exposure.
action: JPMorgan customers: be wary of unexpected emails that mention your account or card.
impact: Some customer names and email addresses may be exposed. Newsweek separately reports that a group called n0n published around 16,000 customer email addresses and phone numbers that appear to relate to Visa's Reserve card program.

validation.note: Newsweek (quotes a JPMorgan spokesman) and Crypto Briefing report independently; vendors not named; the 16,000 figure and n0n are Newsweek's account and relate to Visa's Reserve program.

review.note: Compared with Newsweek, Crypto Briefing, ABC13: post became statement; removed unsourced customer-contact line; 16,000 is n0n per Newsweek (emails and phone numbers, Visa Reserve data), not JPMorgan-confirmed; added no date or vendor names.
